title: Bigfoot Festival prepares to return to West Virginia in 2026

content:
SUMMERSVILLE, WV (WVNS) -- Cryptid-loving fans will have a chance to enjoy cryptid-related entertainment as the Bigfoot Festival prepares to return to the Mountain State in 2026.

According to a press release, from October 9, 2026 through October 11, 2026, the West Virginia Bigfoot Festival will make its way to the Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in the Summersville area where cryptid fans will be able to enjoy a variety of activities. Admission to the 2026 Bigfoot Festival will be $10.

 Mothman Festival to return for 2026 

The press release stated that attendees will be able to enjoy live music, bigfoot research, family activities, Appalachian entertainment, and "some of the most recognizable personalities in the world of cryptozoology and paranormal television."

According to the press release from the West Virginia Bigfoot Museum, the 2026 Bigfoot Festival will allow a variety of people, such as families, vendors, musicians, researchers, Bigfoot enthusiasts, and television personalities from throughout the Mountain State, as well as from out-of-state.

The 2026 Speakers Barn will include a wide variety of guests, such as "Dr. Mireya Mayor, primatologist, explorer and television personality known to audiences from Expedition Bigfoot; cryptozoologist and author Ken Gerhard; Turtleman; Willy and Jeff from Mountain Monsters; Diamond Jim Boardwine; Mike Familant; Les O'Dell; Charlie Raymond; Sherri Blake and numerous other researchers and presenters," the release stated.

According to the press release, Dr. Mireya Mayor will have two appearances on Saturday: an extended presentation from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and a session from 6:15 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Once the scheduled presentations are over, stories will continue with special evening campfire stories on Friday with Jeff and Willy from Mountain Monsters and Diamond Jim Boardwine; on Saturday with Turtleman; and on Sunday with RPG from Expedition Bigfoot.

The press release stated that Raelyn Nelson Band, The Travelers, Micah Kesselring, Tesa Marie, Shawn Benfield, Thomas Danley, Ben Jamn, Persuaded, and Johnny Spolarich will be some of the entertainment on the Music Stage at the Bigfoot Festival.

 What is a cryptid? 

According to the Bigfoot Museum's press release, the Bigfoot Calling Contest will return for all three days of the festival, and will let attendees find out who can make the most convincing Bigfoot call. At 11:00 a.m. on Sunday, a church service and then live music, will take place at the Music Stage.

The press release stated that a variety of activities, such as a carved pumpkin contest, bounce houses, chainsaw carving, Bigfoot Gem Mining, historic demonstrations by the Bulltown Historic Area, and the River Walk Animal Hunt, will be held throughout the weekend at the Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park. An APW Wrestling Exhibition, Gauley River Cloggers Performance, and a beard contest will be held on Saturday.

Bigfoot lore will be combined with music, family entertainment, Appalachian history, and outdoor adventure as a way to make an event that people who want to experience an "unusual West Virginia weekend," as well as fans of Bigfoot will be able to enjoy, according to the release.

The press release from the Bigfoot Museum stated that additional information, updates, and announcements can be found on the Bigfoot Festival's Facebook page.
